text: {"answer":"The passages give a mixed picture, so a blanket daily recommendation for all adults is not clearly supported. Supplementation reliably corrects deficiency and improves bone mineral density in adults with low baseline serum levels, which supports daily use in that group [vitamin_d#0]. Deficient populations also show better muscle strength and fall rates after daily supplementation [vitamin_d#3]. A meta-analysis reports a modest fracture benefit in older adults when vitamin D is combined with calcium [vitamin_d#1]. In contrast, a Cochrane review found no reduction in all-cause mortality in adults who are not deficient at baseline [vitamin_d#5], and the VITAL trial found no significant effect on cardiovascular events or cancer [vitamin_d#4]. Routine supplementation in adequate-level populations showed no measurable outcome improvement and adds cost and pill burden [vitamin_d#6]. High doses have been linked to hypercalcaemia and, in some trials, to increased fall risk [vitamin_d#7]. Observational links to fewer infections are associational only [vitamin_d#2]. Overall, daily use seems most justified for deficient adults.","confidence":60,"one_line":"Daily vitamin D helps mainly deficient adults; routine use in adequate-level adults shows no clear outcome benefit and high doses carry risks."}
